adc3bbd04b39dfd993f8483a7b6dacf2c4304a65.summary: Sekoia Threat Detection & Research describes FakeBat (also called EugenLoader or PaykLoader), a loader sold as Malware-as-a-Service since at least December 2022 and one of the most widespread drive-by download loaders in the first half of 2024. Distribution clusters include malvertising with software impersonation, fake browser updates injected into compromised websites, and a social engineering campaign against the web3 community. The report covers operator activity on cybercrime forums, pricing, distribution clusters and tracking of C2 infrastructure, and it shares IoCs and YARA rules.

adc6c259bb0270e22e83f63cea05797cf0b5a8cc.summary: Trend Micro article on the Erebus ransomware and its Linux variant. Erebus first emerged in September 2016, spread through malvertisements and the Rig exploit kit, and later used a User Account Control bypass. The Linux version infected 153 servers at South Korean web hosting company NAYANA in June, affecting around 3,400 businesses. The report says NAYANA appears to have paid a first ransom payment but has not received a decryption key. It also gives server hardening advice.

ad6740045c5dc9af006d2517ce6f8b17bda5a79d.summary: ESET describes two Linux backdoors. It attributes WolfsBane to the Gelsemium APT group with high confidence, and FireWood to Gelsemium with low confidence, as a possible tool shared by China-aligned groups. Samples came from archives uploaded to VirusTotal from Taiwan, the Philippines and Singapore, probably from an incident response on a compromised server. The archives also held web shells, a trojanized SSH client and a privilege escalation helper. ESET concludes with medium confidence that initial access was an unknown web application vulnerability.

ad5861dd889241147f29105b1e93ce68d73dc5ad.summary: A hosting-company blog post for server administrators. It lists Linux log files worth monitoring, such as the system, authentication, kernel, cron, package, mail, Apache and MySQL logs, and recommends centralized log monitoring. It describes no threat actor, campaign, malware, vulnerability or incident, so it is not a threat report.

ad6a75c66b13ba9b3bf0b3ee2e286d66fe8aa1b4.summary: CloudSEK analysis of the files used in an ESXiArgs ransomware attack on VMware ESXi servers. Threat actors exploit CVE-2021-21974, a heap-overflow in OpenSLP, for remote code execution. A Bash script prepares virtual machines and runs a GCC-compiled binary that encrypts their files with RSA and the Sosemanuk stream cipher. It leaves a ransom note, deletes logs and alters files to hide traces. The report says more than 3200 organisations were infected, though the number of vulnerable servers is hard to ascertain. The files were shared by a forum member on 03 February 2023.
